title: What Are Pipes? 🔧
description: Learn how pipes transform display data in templates with zero component logic.

slides.title: Data Display Made Simple 🖥️
slides.content:
# Pipes: Template Transformers

A **pipe** is a simple function that takes a value and returns a transformed version for display.

* Used directly in the template with the `|` (pipe) operator.
* They don’t change the original data – only how it appears.
* Angular ships with many built‑in pipes (Date, Currency, UpperCase, etc.).
* You can chain pipes: `{{ birthday | date | uppercase }}`.

quizData.question: What symbol is used to apply a pipe in Angular?
quizData.explanation: The pipe character `|` triggers a pipe transformation.

slides.title: Parameters – Pipes Can Take Arguments ⚙️
slides.content:
Many pipes accept parameters separated by colons:

```html
{{ birthday | date:'longDate' }}
{{ price | currency:'EUR':'symbol' }}
```

* The first argument after `:` is the format or main parameter.
* Additional arguments follow with more colons.
* Parameters can also be dynamic (component properties): `dateFormat`.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Pipes are Pure (by default)

A pure pipe runs only when the input value changes (primitive) or the object reference changes (object). This makes them efficient. We’ll explore pure vs impure later.

quizData.question: To apply multiple pipes, you separate them with the ____ symbol.
quizData.explanation: Chaining uses multiple `|` e.g., `{{ value | pipe1 | pipe2 }}`.
